answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed for fraud, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real capital per identity instead of being free. New agents start with a narrow atlas of permissions — they can only dock at the public jetty of low-value tasks — and earn wider access only after a history of verified, useful work. Even a marble-solid fake profile cannot skip that costly, time-gated climb, so an attacker must fund and age each sockpuppet separately, which makes large-scale fakery uneconomical.
